output.summary: KEP-3243 proposes a MatchLabelKeys field in TopologySpreadConstraint so that pod topology spreading is computed per Deployment revision during rolling upgrades. Its current status is implementable, stage beta.
output.rationale: Topology spread constraints use a label selector that matches pods across all ReplicaSets of a Deployment, so during a rollout old and new pods skew the distribution. The KEP has kube-apiserver merge label values from the listed keys into the LabelSelector at pod creation, and kube-scheduler handles the same keys for cluster-level default constraints. Reviewers asked for an upgrade path in which kube-scheduler handles all incoming pods during the transition release.

alternatives.option: Implement MatchLabelKeys only inside the PodTopologySpread scheduler plugin
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this may confuse users because it would differ from PodAffinity's MatchLabelKeys, and it cannot be applied to the update path cleanly.
The KEP says this would make it impossible to handle matchLabelKeys in the cluster-level default constraints in the scheduler configuration.

alternatives.option: Use a manual revision label on the Deployment and update the selector at each rollout
alternatives.why_not: The Motivation section calls this not user friendly and error prone, requiring manual tuning.

alternatives.option: Run a descheduler to rebalance pods
alternatives.why_not: The Motivation section says it requires installing and maintaining an extra controller.

evidence.quote: The main case that this new way for identifying pods will enable is constraining skew spreading calculation to happen at the revision level in Deployments during rolling upgrades.
The root cause is that PodTopologySpread constraints allow defining a key-value label selector, which applies to all pods in a Deployment irrespective of their owning ReplicaSet.
we cannot implement this feature only within kube-apiserver because it'd make it impossible to handle `matchLabelKeys` within the cluster-level default constraints in the scheduler configuration.
So, for a safe upgrade path from v1.32 to v1.33, kube-scheduler would handle not only `matchLabelKeys` from the default constraints, but also all incoming pods during v1.33.
OK, I've merged this change into #5205 and close this PR.
